items.title: Master AI or AI will master us, Anwar tells youth
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian youth must master emerging technologies, particularly artificial intelligence (AI), to ensure the country keeps pace with rapid global change, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. He said mastering new technologies could reshape the way young people think, live and participate in the economy of the future. Anwar said a new generation equipped with knowledge, discipline and strong values could help propel Malaysia towards greater progress.

items.title: Anwar recalls childhood lesson on stealing, tells youths to reject corruption
items.summary: Anwar said young people should retain their idealism and refuse to tolerate corruption. Anwar said his grandmother questioned him after he returned home with the fruits and told him that taking something without permission amounted to stealing. "My grandmother said, 'Anwar, if you take something without permission from anyone, even four nutmegs, that is stealing.

items.title: 690 terrapin hatchlings released into Sungai Kemaman to boost conservation
items.summary: CHUKAI: Some 690 terrapin hatchlings were released into their natural habitat in Sungai Kemaman near Kampung Pasir Gajah here today. Chen said the terrapin hatchlings were released in stages, with today's release marking the completion of this year's programme. Last year, 680 terrapin hatchlings were released into the river.

items.title: 'Don't make us second victims': Nepal flood families demand central bank debt relief
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Families of the 54 Malaysians still unaccounted for after the Nepal flash floods and landslides have welcomed Bank Negara Malaysia's (BNM) readiness to facilitate financial assistance, but want a single, centrally coordinated framework. Malaysia Solidarity: Families in Hope (MASFIH) spokesman Dr Manivannan Rethinam said BNM's indication that financial institutions may consider repayment deferments, fee and charge waivers, documentation flexibility and expedited insurance and takaful claims was a positive step. Manivannan said BNM's move was welcome after what the families described as 39 days of uncertainty, anguish and unanswered questions.

items.title: Sultan of Brunei arrives as Sepang hosts surprise F1 GP
items.summary: SUBANG JAYA, Oct 3 — The Sultan of Brunei, Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah, arrived in Malaysia today for a special visit in conjunction with the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC), which began yesterday. The special aircraft carrying His Majesty and the Brunei delegation, including Prince Abdul Mateen Bolkiah, landed safely at the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) base in Subang at 4.28pm. The Sepang International Circuit has been selected to host the 2026 F1 Gulf Air Bahrain GP, making the iconic circuit a temporary venue for the prestigious race.

items.title: 77-year-old man feared drowned was due to remarry in December
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI: A 77-year-old man who was feared drowned after his car plunged into a river in Lubuk Kawah last night was supposed to remarry on Dec 12. His son, Muhamad Noor, 43, said the family had accepted the incident and was hoping his father would be found soon. Nisun said she hoped Mat Yusof would be found as soon as possible.

items.title: Manager held three more days over alleged RM200m tax reduction fraud
items.summary: The media previously reported that preliminary investigations found the suspect was believed to have manipulated approximately 480 company accounts using fraudulent documents between 2018 and this year. During the operation, the MACC seized 25 luxury vehicles estimated to be worth approximately RM25 million. The MACC also froze seven bank accounts, comprising four personal accounts and three company accounts, with a total value of approximately RM3 million.

items.title: Melaka polls: Pakatan to announce candidates in one or two weeks, says Amirudin
items.summary: KLANG, Oct 3 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) is expected to announce its candidates for the Melaka state election within the next one or two weeks, says PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. On September 27, Melaka PH confirmed that seat distribution among its component parties at the state level for the Melaka state election had been completed. Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari was reported as saying that the final seat arrangement, however, would be concluded following discussions among the PH Presidential Council, state PH leadership, and Amirudin as PH election director.

items.title: Doctor loses RM300,000 in fake student investment scheme
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A private medical practitioner lost RM300,000 after falling victim to an investment scam involving a non-existent Kad Prihatin Siswa project. Ampang Jaya police chief Assistant Commissioner Khairul Anuar Khalid said the victim, a 38-year-old local woman, and her husband began dealing with a male suspect over the purported project in early 2023. Khairul Anuar said an investment agreement was subsequently signed between the victim and the suspect, promising returns of 10 per cent a month for 12 months.

items.title: Bahrain F1 Grand Prix: Spectators complain about expensive food, drinks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Food and beverage prices at Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) have sparked discussion online after several spectators shared their experiences on social media. A Threads user, @myk3_mash, also questioned the alleged RM50 price of Chinese fried rice. I can't afford it," said user @daripadakeme.gifts.

items.title: Time for a review: Creative industry seeks more Budget 2027 support as TV production rates lag behind costs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Creative industry players are calling on the government to maintain and enhance existing funds and incentives in the upcoming Budget 2027, while reviewing television programme production rates, which they say are no longer realistic amid rising costs. Malaysian Film Producers Association deputy president Datuk Dr Yusof Haslam said government incentives and assistance should be maintained without cuts to safeguard the sustainability of the local creative industry ecosystem. On the Film in Malaysia Incentive (FIMI), Yusof said the initiative has not only succeeded in attracting international production companies but has also provided crucial support for large-scale patriotic productions such as ‘MALBATT: Misi Bakara’.

items.title: Maintenance worker dies after being electrocuted while repairing house roof
items.summary: Cheng Gwo Pyng, 49, a maintenance worker, became unconscious after being electrocuted while on the roof of the house. Kuala Muda district police chief Assistant Commissioner Hanyan Ramlan confirmed the incident and said the case had been classified as sudden death. "Police received a report on the incident about 11.35am today," he said.

items.title: PH to announce Melaka election candidates within 2 weeks, says Amirudin
items.summary: KLANG: Pakatan Harapan (PH) is expected to announce its candidates for the Melaka election within the next two weeks, said PH election director Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari. He said PH had been preparing for the 16th Melaka election for about two months, including meetings with its election machinery and teams. "Preparations have been ongoing for the past two months, including meetings with our election machinery and teams.

items.title: Malaysia cuts use of ozone-depleting HCFC by nearly 80pc, eyes full phase-out by 2030
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 3 — The National World Ozone Day 2026 celebration has reinforced Malaysia’s commitment to protecting the ozone layer and tackling climate change through a transition towards more sustainable and energy-efficient cooling technologies. In a statement today, the Department of Environment (DOE) said the celebration, officiated by DOE Deputy Director-General (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon at a shopping centre here, carried the theme “Global Action for a Cooler Planet: Celebrating 10 Years of Sustainable Cooling under the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol”. “Malaysia, which ratified the Montreal Protocol in 1989, completely phased out chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and Halons in 2010.

items.title: [UPDATED] Anwar hints 2027 Budget will address financial hardship among university students
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has hinted that the 2027 Budget will include measures to address financial hardship among university students, including those struggling with hunger and debt. Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the unity government had always listened to the aspirations and concerns of youths, particularly those pursuing higher education. Young people today, in the current narrative, are of course the leaders of the future, but young people today must also help and lead the country.

items.title: Police arrest motorcyclist for riding against traffic, crashing into two KL marathon participants
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — A 21-year-old motorcyclist was arrested after allegedly riding against traffic and crashing into two participants of the Kuala Lumpur Standard Chartered Marathon (KLSCM) 2026 along Jalan Munshi Abdullah early today. Kuala Lumpur Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department chief ACP Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the incident occurred at about 6.15am after the motorcyclist, who was carrying a 19-year-old pillion rider, allegedly passed through a road closure marked by cones. Lee Traffic Police Station at 03-2071 9999 or the nearest police station.

items.title: [UPDATED] Bandar Utama schoolgirl's family sues govt, others over her death
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The mother and sister of Yap Shing Xuen, who was killed on Oct 14 last year, have filed a civil suit in the Kuala Lumpur High Court against several parties over her death. In a statement, the mother said the suit, filed on Oct 1 through Messrs Surendra Ananth, named several government agencies, the parents of the boy who killed Yap and the boy himself as defendants. She said the family believed Yap's death could have been prevented had the relevant parties taken appropriate steps, particularly in addressing mental health issues among students.

items.title: Bahrain F1 Grand Prix: Spectators told not to cut queues
items.summary: SEPANG: Spectators attending the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia and road users around the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) here should follow the instructions of police on duty to ensure smooth movement in and out of the venue. KLIA police chief Assistant Commissioner M Ravi said police and all relevant parties had made thorough preparations to ensure the main event tomorrow ran smoothly. He said road users around SIC were also asked to cooperate and comply with the diversions and road closures implemented in the area to ease traffic flow.

items.title: Financial institutions ready to assist families of Nepal flood victims
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Financial service providers stand ready to extend appropriate relief and support to the families of victims affected by the recent floods along the Nepal-China border, in line with applicable laws and regulatory requirements, said Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM). BNM advised the next of kin of affected Malaysians to reach out to the relevant financial institutions for appropriate assistance. The central bank said it would work closely with financial institutions to ensure the timely provision of support to those affected by the tragedy.

items.title: Replacing cancelled Norway missiles could cost Malaysia over RM1bil
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: Procuring a new surface-to-surface missile system after Malaysia's Naval Strike Missile (NSM) deal with Norway was cancelled could cost the government more than RM1 billion. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said fresh funding was needed for replacement missiles as the navy's warships could not be left without a primary missile system. He said the Norwegian government had refused to advance a refund for payments already made by Malaysia, forcing the Defence Ministry to consider suppliers from three other countries.

items.title: Family of Bandar Utama school stabbing victim files civil suit against government agencies, boy and his parents
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — The mother and sister of the 16-year-old student who was fatally stabbed at a secondary school in Bandar Utama last year have filed a civil suit at the Kuala Lumpur High Court. The family’s lawyer, Surendra Ananth, confirmed the suit that was filed on Thursday, adding that case management has been fixed for October 29. At the time, the family said it planned to pursue a civil suit as the criminal case moved to the appeal stage following the Shah Alam High Court’s decision to acquit the teenage accused on the grounds of unsoundness of mind.

items.title: MAF to rebalance personnel deployment between peninsula, Sabah and Sarawak
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: The government will restructure the deployment of Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) personnel between Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak to ensure a more balanced concentration of defence assets, said Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin. He said the government was targeting an even split, with 50 per cent of MAF personnel stationed in the peninsula and the remaining 50 per cent in Sabah and Sarawak. Currently, about two-thirds of MAF personnel are deployed in the peninsula, while the remaining one-third are stationed in Sabah and Sarawak, totalling about 20,000 personnel at any given time.

items.title: Malaysian pilot detained in Jakarta over alleged drug smuggling gets another 30 days in custody
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — The 39-year-old Malaysia Airlines pilot arrested in Jakarta in July over an alleged drug-smuggling operation remains in Indonesian custody after authorities extended his detention beyond the initial 60-day period. Harian Metro reported today that Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the extension was for another 30 days. “The Malaysian police were informed by the Indonesian narcotics authorities.

items.title: Drunk motorcyclist crashes into 2 marathon runners in KL
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A motorcyclist who allegedly rode through a road closure before travelling against traffic crashed into two Standard Chartered Kuala Lumpur Marathon (SCKLM) 2026 participants early today. Kuala Lumpur Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Zamzuri Mohd Isa said the incident occurred at Jalan Munshi Abdullah about 6.15am. Lee Traffic Police Station at 03-2071 9999 or the nearest police station.

items.title: Police detonate three mortar bombs found among scrap metal in Dengkil
items.summary: SEPANG: Police detonated three mortar bombs this morning, a day after they were found among scrap metal outside a house in Dengkil. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Norhizam Bahaman said the bombs, one measuring 81mm and two measuring 60mm, were destroyed by the police Bomb Disposal Unit at an open construction site in Dengkil about 9.20am. The Bomb Disposal Unit was called in and confirmed that the objects were mortar bombs before removing them to a safe location for disposal.

items.title: Abang Johari: The time will come for me to step down
items.summary: MUKAH: Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Abang Openg says the time will come for him to step down, describing it as a "natural process". Abang Johari said his age and health would be the primary considerations, adding that this was why it was important to prepare the next line of experienced leaders to ensure continuity in Sarawak's development. Abang Johari said it took a team to lead a state and that every member must prepare well-trained successors.

items.title: Military build-up on Philippine island risks conflict spillover to nearby Malaysia, says Khaled Nordin
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Oct 3 — Malaysia does not view the military build-up on the southern Philippine island of Balabac as a direct threat, said Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin. The defence minister said it was the Philippines’ right and prerogative to cooperate with the US military to strengthen its defence capabilities. On a separate matter, Mohamed Khaled said the government aims to achieve a 50-50 ratio in the deployment of Malaysian Armed Forces (MAF) personnel between Peninsular Malaysia and Sabah and Sarawak.

items.title: Sepang International Circuit working with partners, authorities to improve F1 traffic management
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 3 — The Sepang International Circuit (SIC) is working closely with its transport partners and relevant authorities to strengthen traffic, shuttle and crowd management arrangements for the Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix (GP) 2026 race. “The experience and safety of our fans remain our highest priority at Sepang International Circuit,” it said in a statement today. A Formula 1 driver is seen during the free practice session for the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit October 2, 2026.

items.title: Man loses RM1.14mil to 'investment' scheme promising 15 per cent returns
items.summary: Pontian police chief Superintendent Hadzrat Hussien Mion Mussain said initial investigations revealed the victim met a woman named "Fairini" via WhatsApp in early January. "On Feb 8, the victim made a trial investment transaction of RM5,000 into a bank account provided by the suspect," he said in a statement. Hadzrat Hussien said following the transaction, the victim received a payout of RM5,877.65, credited to his account as returns.

items.title: Towards A Better Medical Dispute Resolution System for Malaysia
items.summary: LETTER: MEDICO-LEGAL complaints in Malaysia's public healthcare system have risen in recent years, increasing from 165 cases in 2021 to 283 in 2023. However, the upward trend presents opportunities for the healthcare sector to strengthen Malaysia's medical dispute resolution system. Even so, these cases play an important role in shaping clinical practice, communication standards, and how patients experience care.

items.title: National service training draws encouraging response as 10 turn up without prior confirmation
items.summary: ALOR STAR: The response to the National Service Training Programme 3.0 (NS 3.0) has been encouraging, with 10 people voluntarily turning up at the 513th Regiment (Territorial Army) National Service Training Camp in Kepala Batas here today, despite not having confirmed their participation in advance. Colonel Abdul Rani Abdul Majid, director of the Policy and Development Division at the National Service Training Department headquarters, said the development indicated that some individuals were interested in joining NS 3.0 after learning more about the programme. In addition, 10 people arrived voluntarily this morning without prior confirmation to apply for the training," he said while observing the registration of NS 3.0 Series 4/2026 trainees here today.

items.title: Premier: Sarawak Budget 2027 to cover electricity tariffs, revenue and economic direction
items.summary: MUKAH, Oct 3 — Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg hinted that the Sarawak Budget 2027, to be tabled at the upcoming State Legislative Assembly (DUN) session, will address various matters, including electricity tariffs, economic direction, and the state’s revenue position. “God willing, I will table the Sarawak Budget in two weeks. And what about Sarawak’s revenue?

items.title: Political journeyman Norhizam ready for another Melaka run
items.summary: MELAKA: Former Pengkalan Batu assemblyman Datuk Norhizam Hassan Baktee says he is ready to contest in the upcoming state election. The Hang Tuah Jaya Bersatu vice-chief said this included the possibility of contesting his former seat. "But I want to serve the people of Pengkalan Batu again," he said when contacted.

items.title: No more RM12.50 medicine delivery fee, but for rural Sabah patients, the bigger savings may be the journey
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 3 — Sabah patients using the Ubat Melalui Pos (UMP) service no longer have to pay the RM12.50 delivery charge from October 1 removing a cost that was more than twice the RM5.70 previously charged in Peninsular Malaysia. Particularly meaningful in Sabah, where patients from rural and interior areas have to travel considerable distances simply to collect repeat medication from hospitals or health clinics. About 87,000 registered UMP patients nationwide are expected to benefit from the free delivery initiative.

items.title: [UPDATED] MACC seizes 25 luxury vehicles worth RM25mil in tax reduction probe
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has seized 25 luxury vehicles worth about RM25 million in connection with an investigation into a company manager suspected of submitting false documents to obtain tax reductions worth about RM200 million. MACC also froze four personal bank accounts and three company accounts containing about RM3 million. The suspect, a company manager at a financial and corporate services agency, is being investigated over allegations of submitting false documents to obtain tax reductions worth about RM200 million.

items.title: Umno ready to discuss Pas' use of BN logo in Melaka polls
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: Umno is prepared to discuss Pas' intention to use the Barisan Nasional logo in the upcoming Melaka election. Umno vice-president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the party welcomed the intention, but any such proposal would have to be discussed through official channels. Asked whether other PN component parties, such as Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan), would also want to use the BN logo, Khaled jokingly said the openness did not extend to every party.

items.title: Young Malaysians show enthusiasm as PLKN 3.0 attracts ten unexpected volunteers in Kepala Batas
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Oct 3 — The response to the National Service Training Programme (PLKN) 3.0 has been encouraging, with 10 individuals voluntarily showing up at the 513th Regiment (Territorial Army) National Service Training Camp (CLKN) in Kepala Batas here today, despite not having made prior confirmation to join the programme. Colonel Abdul Rani Abdul Majid, director of the Policy and Development Division at the National Service Training Department (JLKN) headquarters, said this development indicates there are individuals interested in joining PLKN 3.0 after learning about the programme. “We had received confirmation from 211 trainees scheduled to register today, additionally, as of this morning, 10 people arrived voluntarily without prior confirmation to apply for the training,” he told Bernama while observing the registration for PLKN 3.0 Series 4/2026 trainees here today.

items.title: Man jailed seven years for misappropriating RM254,000 in company funds
items.summary: MIRI: A man was sentenced to seven years in jail, fined RM20,000 and ordered to receive one stroke of the rotan after pleading guilty to misappropriating more than RM254,000 in company funds. Miri police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Farhan Lee Abdullah said the 36-year-old man, who worked for the company, was entrusted with the money on Sept 18. "Instead of paying the staff, the man used the funds for personal expenses, including online gambling," Farhan said in a statement.

items.title: ‘Use official complaints channel’: Fahmi urges public to report ethical media concerns to Malaysian Media Council
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 3 — Members of the public who have complaints regarding the ethics of local media reporting can channel them to the Malaysian Media Council (MMM), said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. Yesterday, the Putrajaya Media Club (KMP) lodged reports with police and the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) regarding a social media post that allegedly edited images of media personnel into images of animals. Elaborating, Fahmi said MCMC had identified several social media accounts found to have disseminated offensive content by misusing artificial intelligence (AI) applications to edit images of Tun Dr Mahathir during the period following Tun Dr Siti Hasmah’s passing.

items.title: Malbatt peacekeepers in Lebanon to return home from January 2027
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: All members of the Malaysian Battalion (Malbatt) currently serving in Lebanon are expected to begin returning home in January 2027, following the conclusion of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (Unifil) mandate at the end of this year. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the withdrawal process would be carried out in stages via several flights, followed by the return of military assets by sea starting Jan 17. In a related development, Khaled said Malaysia was prepared to consider participating in a new peacekeeping force in Lebanon should the United Nations (UN) request it.

items.title: Doctor couple lose RM300k after being duped by father of former singer
items.summary: The victim, who wished to be known as Dr Alia, 38, said the man claimed to have connections with senior government officials and told them that minutes of meetings on the project had been submitted to the government. Dr Alia said she knew the Datuk as the son-in-law of one of her patients. She said the couple invested RM300,000 in the project in August 2023.

items.title: ‘Dedicated lanes, smooth queues’: F1 fans praise improved crowd and traffic management at Sepang Circuit
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 3 — Formula 1 (F1) fans have praised the improved crowd and traffic management at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) here today, following congestion and long queues reported after yesterday’s opening day of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia 2026. A Threads user, @tanissha_.26, commended the arrangements, particularly the dedicated lanes and improved coordination for shuttle buses. Dedicated lane for shuttle buses.

items.title: Immigration arrests 37,313 undocumented migrants in nine months
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Immigration Department carried out 10,374 enforcement operations nationwide and arrested 37,313 undocumented migrants between Jan 1 and Sept 29 this year. He said enforcement also targeted employers suspected of hiring or harbouring undocumented migrants. Saifuddin said the Home Ministry and Immigration Department would continue conducting enforcement operations daily.

items.title: Rapid KL: Sepang shuttle arrangements improved for Day 2 of Bahrain GP after feedback
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Rapid KL said it has improved shuttle bus arrangements at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) today following complaints from Formula One spectators over long queues and delays yesterday. Rapid KL said that as of 11am, traffic and passenger movements were smooth and under control, adding that it would continue monitoring the situation with SIC and the relevant agencies. “Following the feedback received, Rapid KL together with SIC and the relevant agencies have made improvements to arrangements at the pick-up and drop-off locations,” it said in a statement.

items.title: Malaysia to begin bringing Malbatt personnel home from Lebanon in January, says defence minister
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Oct 3 — All members of the Malaysian Battalion (Malbatt) currently serving in Lebanon are expected to begin returning home in January 2027, following the conclusion of the United Nations Interim Force in Lebanon (Unifil) mandate at the end of this year. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the withdrawal process for the personnel would be carried out in stages via several flights, followed by the return of military assets by sea starting January 17. “Our personnel are expected to start returning next January on several flights, while Malaysian military assets will be brought back by ship starting January 17,” he said at a press conference following the groundbreaking ceremony for the Kota Tinggi Muslim Orphanage here today.

items.title: Car pulled from river after plunging in, but 77-year-old driver still missing near Sungai Petani
items.summary: SUNGAI PETANI, Oct 3 — A 77-year-old man remains missing after the car he was driving is believed to have skidded and plunged into a river along Jalan Lubuk Segintah-Lubuk Kawah near here early today. Kuala Muda police chief ACP Hanyan Ramlan said that in the incident, which occurred at about 1am, Mat Yusof Hashim was believed to have been driving a Proton Wira from Jalan Kuala Ketil towards Felda Teloi Timur. “As such, the Fire and Rescue Department is continuing the search and rescue operation for the victim in the surrounding river area,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Ranau records weak 3.5-magnitude earthquake, tremors felt in surrounding areas
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 3 — A weak earthquake measuring 3.5 on the Richter scale occurred in the Panginatan area of Ranau at 10.57am today. The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said the earthquake’s epicentre was detected at coordinates 5.9° North and 116.7° East, at a depth of 13 kilometres. According to MetMalaysia, the epicentre was located approximately 14 kilometres south of Ranau.

items.title: Khaled Nordin: PAS can discuss using BN logo for Melaka polls, but door not open to all Perikatan parties
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI, Oct 3 — Umno wil be selective in permitting parties under Perikatan Nasional (PN) from using Barisan Nasional’s (BN) logo should they agree to a political cooperation for the upcoming Melaka state election, said party vice president Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin. He said that only parties deemed acceptable would be allowed to use the BN logo, with only PAS having expressed such an intention “We have not discussed the matter yet. On the possibility of Parti Wawasan Negara (Wawasan) contesting under BN due to potential logo restrictions following the Registrar of Societies’ (RoS) recent suspension of the coalition, Mohamed Khaled said BN and Umno welcomes any party that support the coalition.

items.title: Army officer arrested at public university with firearm, preliminary test positive for ketum compound
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — The Malaysian Army (TDM) has confirmed that all firearms and ammunition in its storage facilities are fully accounted for following the arrest of an army officer at a public university on September 28. TDM reiterated its commitment to cooperating fully with the authorities and taking appropriate action should any regulatory violations be confirmed by the investigation findings. “Any conclusions regarding the incident must be based on facts and the authorities’ investigation findings, rather than unverified information.

items.title: Negeri Sembilan seeks federal support for roads, water security and disaster preparedness in Budget 2027
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 3 — Strengthening critical infrastructure, boosting water security and enhancing disaster preparedness are among Negeri Sembilan’s key priorities put forward for the Federal Government’s consideration in Budget 2027. He said Federal Government support would help lay a strong foundation for the state’s medium- and long-term development. Ismail said the development proposals were in line with Negeri Sembilan’s long-term development plan for 2026-2035, which emphasises economic and social growth, sustainability and inclusive development.

items.title: MCMC: Meta confirms technical error wrongfully suspended WhatsApp accounts in Malaysia
items.summary: In a statement today, MCMC said it had received feedback from Meta regarding the issue of WhatsApp account suspensions that had previously been brought to the company’s attention. “According to Meta, the technical error was addressed at the end of September and affected legitimate accounts were proactively restored, including some accounts that had not submitted appeals. MCMC said that for other cases, Meta explained that account suspensions could involve several factors, including recycled phone numbers previously associated with blocked accounts, spam or scam activity, and usage patterns detected by WhatsApp’s security systems.

items.title: Banks and insurers ready to offer relief to families affected by Nepal-China floods, says BNM
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Financial service providers stand ready to extend appropriate relief and support to the families of the victims affected by the recent floods along the Nepal-China border, in line with applicable laws and regulatory requirements, said Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM). The central bank said that assistance or goodwill measures may include repayment deferments, waivers of fees and charges, and flexibility in documentation requirements pending the completion of the relevant legal processes. BNM advised next of kin of the affected Malaysians to reach out to the relevant financial institutions for appropriate assistance.

items.title: Perak floods displace 58 people, two relief centres opened
items.summary: The State Disaster Management Committee Secretariat said all the victims had been placed at the PPS at Dewan Orang Ramai Kampung Degong in Hilir Perak and the PPS at Kampung Menteri Mosque in Larut, Matang and Selama. “The PPS at Dewan Orang Ramai Kampung Degong is sheltering three victims following floods in the Jalan Kampar-Langkap area at 4pm last Thursday. “The PPS at Kampung Menteri Mosque, meanwhile, is sheltering 55 victims from 15 families following floods in the Kampung Menteri area at 8pm yesterday,” it said in a statement today.

items.title: Man killed, family injured in Port Dickson crash involving lorry driver allegedly over alcohol limit
items.summary: PORT DICKSON, Oct 3 — A man was killed while his wife and daughter were injured after the Perodua Myvi they were travelling in collided with a lorry driven by a man suspected to be under the influence of alcohol at KM13.5 of Jalan Lukut-Sepang here yesterday. Port Dickson district police chief Supt Ahmad Afiq Mohd Adnan said the 35-year-old car driver died at the scene due to severe injuries in the 6.50pm incident, while his 32-year-old wife and their five-year-old daughter sustained injuries. “The lorry driver was unhurt.

items.title: Malaysian listed as ‘uncontactable’ after Nepal floods returns home safely, 54 still missing
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 3 — A Malaysian previously reported as uncontactable following floods and landslides in Nepal has returned safely to Malaysia, the Foreign Ministry said today. “Following his return, the relevant authorities in Malaysia will record a statement from the individual to complete the official record concerning his case,” it said in a statement. “With his status now confirmed, the Ministry’s record stands at 54 Malaysians reported as uncontactable,” Wisma Putra said.

items.title: Malaysia eyes role in Brazilian aircraft maker Embraer’s global supply chain
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Malaysia is exploring cooperation with Embraer Defense & Security of Brazil to join the company’s regional and global supply chain. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the matter was discussed during a courtesy call by the company’s chief commercial officer, Frederico Lemos, at Wisma Pertahanan yesterday. He said Embraer has expertise in aircraft development and integrated defence solutions.

items.title: Four areas in Johor and Sarawak still in unhealthy API range, Sri Aman highest at 152
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Four areas in Johor and Sarawak recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 9am today. According to data from the Department of Environment’s (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Sri Aman in Sarawak recorded the highest reading at 152, followed by Pasir Gudang, Johor (151). Meanwhile, 61 areas recorded moderate readings, while two areas were classified as having favourable air quality - Taiping, Perak (44) and Temerloh, Pahang (42).

items.title: Bahrain GP in Malaysia: F1 fans complain of gridlocked traffic, over three-hour waits for shuttles
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 3 — Formula 1 spectators have complained of gridlocked roads, long shuttle bus queues and poor crowd management at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC), after the first day of the Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia yesterday. Malaysian X user @tuakdotsol, said this morning that roads heading towards the circuit remained gridlocked, while private cars and e-hailing vehicles were apparently being stopped at the perimeter, funnelling spectators towards shuttle hubs at Mitsui Outlet Park and KLIA Terminal 2. “Apparently private cars and Grabs are blocked at the perimeter, so everyone funnels into shuttle hubs at Mitsui outlet and KLIA T2,” the user wrote, alongside images showing large crowds near the circuit.
